Summary:

The Prophecy of DELTARUNE tells of seven legendary fountains that will need the power of seven human SOULs to be sealed. Join Kris, Susie, their friends, and six other humans as they work together to save the world… and banish the ANGEL. Grouptale but in Deltarune. Sequel/spinoff to Grouptale.

Chapter 1: Chapter 1, Part 1 - The Angel

Notes:

A/N: Hi folks! Here’s the first chapter of the revamped Deltagroup. This is a spiritual sequel to my Undertale fic Grouptale but you don’t need to read it. You can if you realllyyyy want to but be prepared for ultimate mega cringe lmao. If you have read Grouptale, the characters here will be a bit different from how they appeared there, including some changed backstories haha. After all Deltarune isn’t an exact sequel to Undertale. As for folks who’ve come from the og Deltagroup, well I won’t spoil all the changes… but I hoped to make the new version more original. Anyway enough yapping, hope you enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

It was right before your eyes: a vessel, shimmering in the dark. It was forming, shifting, a voice booming all around you.

You said it was beautiful. It was kind. It liked sour things.

Its appearance shifted, from grey to green to blue and pink. One moment, it was long and tall, then short and squat, and it kept changing, its limbs reshaping, its clothing growing and shrinking, its hair dancing around in the void. It was your creation. You were so proud.

Your eyes were drawn to the SOUL at its center. It was glowing, a beautiful, aching red. You watched in wonder as the SOUL then began to change colour, shifting to cyan, to orange, to green, continuing the rainbow. Its light was spread all around. Just by staring at it, you could feel its power. It was the Angel. You were the Angel, your power shifting and changing.

Then your vessel was discarded.

You could not choose your fate. You couldn't feel your hand.

Everything went black.

...

...

I felt a tugging at my chest.

I couldn't see a thing. Cold, thick darkness surrounded me. I took a deep breath.

I clenched my hands over my heart; a cyan SOUL emerged. It glowed in front of me, radiating with power. I was entranced; the soft shimmer surrounded me, almost like a hug. It was warm and patient, unexpectedly calming. I was comfortable. I wanted to stay like that, forever.

"YOUR TIME IS RUNNING OUT, FAYE RIBSON."

I peered into the darkness. I couldn't see the source of the voice, but I could feel It. I could feel It down to my core, to my very heart. It was watching me. Holding me.

"USE THE POWER YOU HAVE BEEN GIVEN," HE told me. "PLAY YOUR ROLE. PROTECT THEM, AND GIVE YOUR SOUL TO THE CAUSE."

I nodded. The darkness kept growing. So, so dark. Darker, yet darker. My eyes burned. The warmth vanished, replaced by the icy cold of reality.

I tried to breathe, but my lungs were deflating, like there was a hole inside them. My skin was freezing, like ice was growing over it. It was so cold. I was so tired. I didn't want to wake up.

My eyes finally opened, greeting the pale timber of the ceiling. I could hear my phone buzzing on my desk. I sat up, slowly, painfully, reaching for it. My joints creaked, making my eyes water.

I hoped my boyfriend, Brayden, was ringing. He often messaged me in the morning, sending a selfie from his cross-country club, or whatever else he was up to. Sometimes Noelle and Jockington would be in the picture, too. Noelle was usually a bit shy, but she always seemed to enjoy herself at the club. It was nice to see her happy, after all she'd been through. Brayden was just like that, uplifting others with his presence alone. His smile was enough to make me feel hope, to make me feel like I mattered. (Which was why I couldn't tell him the truth...)

Sadly, he was out of town for the day, going to his sister's wedding. I was on my own.

My face fell when I saw the actual caller ID. I didn't want to pick up the phone. I didn't want to talk about that.

I knew I couldn't avoid it forever, though. At some point, I'd have to answer the phone.

But for the moment... if I could wait, so could she. I slowly dragged myself out of bed. It was getting harder to move each day, both physically and emotionally. Before long, I wouldn't be able to move much longer. At least I actually got to sleep at home for the night... but I knew I'd have to go back to the hospital before long.

I reached out, grabbing my medication off my bedside desk. I counted out the small, white tablets, grabbing the glass of water beside them. I swallowed, before sitting back on my bed, closing my eyes once again. I was glad my mattress was so soft. I could sit there all day.

I gazed over at the other side of the room. My sibling, Kris, was still asleep. Despite my sluggish body, they somehow still managed to out-sleep me. Our brother, Asriel, wasn't here to drag them out of bed, and even if I tried, they wouldn't listen to me.

I heard a knock on our door. Mom invited herself in, opening the curtains.

"Kris, Faye, time to wake up," she chorused, "or you will be late for school!"

She turned to Kris, who walked out of bed. Immediately, I knew it wasn't them. Their walk was strangely stiff, their arms glued to their sides. Their footsteps were too noisy. Chapter 2: Chapter 1, Part 2 - The Dark World

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

The floor was cold. You opened your eyes.

You were controlling Kris. You tried to switch to your other vessel, but narration stated there was 'only darkness'.

You saw Melody beside you, and a shining star ahead. A shining star, that reminded you of a world you'd been before...

You reached out, and you SAVED.

I woke up in a bed. Good news, it wasn't a hospital bed. Bad news, it was somewhere I'd never been before.

The walls were black stone, lit up by beautiful, flaming blue torches. My bed was incredibly soft; easily the comfiest bed I'd ever slept on. I could've kept sleeping.

I heard soft footsteps; a hooded, cloaked figure was approaching. I couldn't see their face. They gasped when they noticed I was awake.

"Oh, you're up!" they said, rushing to my side. "How are you feeling?"

"No worse than usual..." I admitted.

"Is there, um, anything you need?" they asked. "Would you like some water? Or something to eat? I just baked a cake!"

"Cake sounds nice," I replied.

The figure hurried out of the room, returning a few moments later with a tray, which held a slice of strawberry sponge cake and a pot of green tea.

They helped by pouring the tea into a mug, then offering it to me.

"Thank you," I said, sipping the tea. It was hot enough to be comforting, but not burning.

"Of course!" the figure said, dipping their head. "I'm... I'm just so glad you're here. It's ever so wonderful to meet you, Faye."

"Who are you?" I asked.

The figure slowly removed their hood, revealing a pitch-black monster-like Darkner, with fluffy ears and glasses. He was wearing a green, witch-like hat, as well as a green robe and a pink scarf.

"Welcome," he said. "I am the Prince of this Kingdom... the KINGDOM of DARKNESS."

"Oh," I breathed.

"My name is Ralsei," he told me. "I hope we can be good friends!"

I offered my free hand for him to shake; his grip was soft and warm, like a teddy bear's. It reminded me of my family.

"What is this place?" I asked him. "This... 'Kingdom of Darkness'?"

"Well..." Ralsei dipped his head. "This is the Dark World, inside the closet. The darkness... created by the hopes and dreams of Lightners."

"I see," I said. "Where is everyone else?"

"I'm not sure," Ralsei admitted. "I'm sure they're on their way, though. I can sense them from the west."

"How did I end up here?" I asked.

"I found you, in the center of town," he said. "You were unconscious, so I brought you inside."

"Oh... " I replied. "Thank you."

"Of course," he smiled, showing fangs. "Anything you need, I'm here to help."

I stared at my hands. My skin was stark white - somehow even more pale than it usually was. I felt my cheek; a bandaid was covering the scar on my cheek. The hair on my shoulder was a dark cyan, almost glimmering in the pale light.

"There is a legend in this land," Ralsei told me. "The legend of DELTARUNE. It tells of... um, well, maybe we should wait until the others get here. Unless you want to hear it now? It's up to you."

"I'm okay with waiting," I said, softly.

Ralsei nodded. "Okay!" He sat on the chair beside my bed. "Um... how's the cake?"

I took a slice of it. It was delicious; creamy and sweet, with the juiciness of the strawberries an added bonus. And yet, it didn't feel very... filling. It was almost like eating cotton-candy; the food simply disappeared as soon as you swallowed.

"It's yummy," I said.

"I'm glad to hear it," Ralsei told me. "Is there anything you'd like? Some more tea?"

"I..." My voice trailed off.

"Oh, am I being too much?" Ralsei stood up. "Sorry. I... I'm a prince, but I don't have any subjects. I... I've just been waiting so long for you and your friends to arrive."

"It's alright," I assured him. "I'm just... I want to enjoy the time I have. That's all." I looked at him. "Us arriving is part of the prophecy, right?"

"Right," Ralsei replied. "Everything
